messages.author: e7601c9255f0ba48
messages.subject: QTL mapping with selective genotyping
parts:
Hi everybody,
Our team plan to do selective genotyping in connected populations for
QTL mapping but this raise a lot questions... Is there some special
procedure implemented in R/QTL to deal with such experiment ? I know
there's one for sgnificance threshold calculation (Manichaikul, 2007)
but what about the procedure proposed by Xu and Vogl (in Heredity,
2000) to map QTL under selective genotyping using only the phenotypic
values of genotyped individuals ?
What about multi-trait and multi-environment QTL mapping ? Is it
possible to map QTL in connected population with R/qtl ?
Regards,
Matthieu

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL mapping with selective genotyping
parts:
I'm not sure what you mean by "connected populations".

Multi-trait analysis is not yet implemented in R/qtl. The case of
multiple environments can be treated by the inclusion of fixed
covariates, but nothing beyond that.

The method of Xu and Vogl (2000) has not been implemented, and I do
not see much reason to do so. It's far better to include, in the
analysis, all phenotyped individuals (including those not genotyped).

karl

messages.author: e7601c9255f0ba48
messages.subject: Re: QTL mapping with selective genotyping
parts:
Just to explain more precisely what I mean by "connected population":
it consists in populations that share parents, as in diallel design.
In our case, the implementation of Xu and Vogl method would have been
interesting because we cannot keep all the populations for
phenotyping. So, we would have only phenotyped and genotyped the
extremes of the ditribution curve. Anyway, thanks a lot for your
answer.
Matthieu
